q: How do I calculate the carbon footprint of a jewellery showroom?
title: Jewellery showroom carbon footprint
short: Read the showroom electricity bill at 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh and add generator diesel at 2.68 kg per litre. Lighting and air conditioning are the main loads, so report per square foot of floor and per month. The jewellery itself sits in Scope 3 as purchased goods.

ul: Air conditioning for the floor and strong room.
Security systems running all day and night.

p: Gold, silver and stones bought for sale are purchased goods in Scope 3, Category 1. Their footprint per gram comes from refiners and suppliers, not from the showroom.
LED display lights and AC set points both show up on the next bills. Compare kWh for the same months year on year, since festive seasons change opening hours.

example.title: Worked example: one showroom (one month, illustrative inputs)
lines: Showroom total: 7,066.6 kg CO2 a month, 84.8 t a year
Per square foot of floor (4,000 sq ft): 1.767 kg CO2 a month
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use the showroom bill and generator fuel slips.

senseible: Senseible reads electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and diesel, LPG and gas invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a dated, fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record for each site. Intensity per unit uses the activity count you enter, and estimates are labelled as estimates.
